dimensions.assessment: Affects financial institutions, banks, and credit unions with assets between $10 billion and $50 billion across the United States.

dimensions.assessment: Exempts financial institutions up to $50 billion in assets from several major federal regulatory frameworks and supervision structures.

dimensions.evidence: To increase the asset thresholds at which financial institutions become subject to certain requirements

summary: H.R. 3230, the Financial Institution Regulatory Tailoring Enhancement Act, increases the asset thresholds from $10 billion to $50 billion at which financial institutions become subject to certain federal regulations, supervision requirements, and rules.

affected_groups.effect: Face supervision by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau at a higher asset threshold of $50 billion instead of $10 billion.
affected_groups.group: Insured depository institutions and credit unions

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with the Volcker Rule at the new higher $50 billion threshold rather than the previous $10 billion threshold.
affected_groups.group: Banks with assets between $10 billion and $50 billion

affected_groups.effect: Qualify for less prescriptive ability-to-repay determinations below the newly raised $50 billion asset level.
Qualify as community banks subject to a simplified leverage ratio if their assets are below the increased $50 billion threshold.
affected_groups.group: Certain depository institutions and depository institution holding companies

key_provisions: Raises the asset level threshold from $10 billion to $50 billion for insured depository institutions and credit unions to fall under supervision by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
Raises the asset level threshold from $10 billion to $50 billion for banks that must comply with the Volcker Rule prohibiting proprietary trading and private fund ownership interests.
Raises the asset level threshold from $10 billion to $50 billion for financial institutions regarding compliance with less prescriptive ability-to-repay determinations for residential mortgages.
Raises the asset level threshold from $10 billion to $50 billion for certain depository institutions and holding companies to qualify as community banks subject to a simplified leverage ratio.
missing_information: Specific numerical estimates of how many banks or credit unions will be affected
Effective implementation dates beyond the legislative text structure
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 3230, the Financial Institution Regulatory Tailoring Enhancement Act, increases the asset thresholds from $10 billion to $50 billion at which financial institutions become subject to certain federal regulations, supervision requirements, and rules.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal oversight by raising specific financial asset thresholds from $10 billion to $50 billion, exempting institutions below that new level from several banking regulations, rules, and supervision types.
